faqs.q: How can I apply for HDFC Freedom Credit Card?
faqs.a: You can apply for this credit card online through the official website of the bank. All you need to do is open the page of this credit card and click on ‘Apply Now’ to fill out the application form. You can also apply offline for this credit card by visiting the nearest branch of the bank and submitting a duly-filled application form.

faqs.q: How can I redeem my HDFC Freedom Credit Card reward points?
faqs.a: You can redeem your earned reward points online via internet banking. You can log in to the internet banking portal and go to the ‘Online Redemption’ and choose the products as per your choice to redeem your reward points. Additionally, you can also redeem your earned reward points offline by posting the rewards redemption form to the HDFC card division.

faqs.q: Can I check my HDFC Freedom Credit Card statement online?
faqs.a: Yes, you can check your credit card statement online by visiting the official website of HDFC Bank. Log in to your account and go to ‘Cards’ section and select the ‘Enquire’ option to view your statement. You can also use HDFC mobile banking app to download your billed statement.

faqs.q: What is the interest rate on HDFC Freedom Credit Card?
faqs.a: In case of default payments, the card charges an annual interest rate of 45%. Besides this, in case of late payments, you have to pay up to Rs. 1,300 as late payment charges according to the outstanding balance.

faqs.q: Should I apply for HDFC Freedom Credit Card as my first credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, HDFC Freedom is an entry-level card designed for consumers who are planning to start their credit journey. You can apply for this card and save on popular brands like Swiggy, BookMyShow, OYO, and Uber.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of choosing the HDFC Freedom Card over other HDFC cards like Millennia?
faqs.a: HDF Freedom is a rewards credit card offering value back in the form of rewards, which you can redeem against multiple categories, along with cash redemption at a value of Rs. 0.15 per point. On the other hand, HDFC Millennia is a cashback card, allowing you to redeem earned CashPoints against cashback at a 1:1 ratio.

faqs.q: What is the annual fee of HDFC Freedom Credit Card?
faqs.a: HDFC Freedom Credit Card charges an annual fee of Rs. 500 + applicable taxes. However, this fee is waived if you spend Rs. 50,000 or more in a year.

faqs.q: Who is eligible for HDFC Freedom Credit Card?
faqs.a: All Indian nationals above the age of 21, whether salaried or self-employed, can apply for this credit card, provided that they meet the income criteria and other card-specific requirements. The maximum age requirement to apply for this credit card is 60 years for salaried applicants and 65 years for self-employed applicants.

faqs.q: What are the benefits of HDFC Freedom Credit Card?
faqs.a: HDFC Freedom is an entry-level credit card that offers basic benefits such as 10X CashPoints on spends made at BigBasket, BookMyShow, OYO, Swiggy, and Uber, and 1 CashPoint for every Rs. 150 spent on other categories. Additionally, the card offers dining discounts through Eazydiner and an additional 10% discount on Swiggy Dineout.

faqs.q: How to redeem HDFC Freedom Credit Card points?
faqs.a: To redeem HDFC Freedom Credit Card reward points, you can log in to your net banking account using your User ID and password. Then, navigate to the Credit Cards section and click on “Redeem Now” to redeem your accumulated reward points from the available options as per your preferences.

faqs.q: What is HDFC Freedom Credit Card?
faqs.a: HDFC Freedom Credit Card is an entry-level card designed for everyday expenses such as dining, groceries, travel, shopping and more. It offers value-back in the form of reward points, which can be redeemed across multiple categories as per your needs.

faqs.q: Is this card suitable for students or first-time credit users?
faqs.a: Yes, HDFC Freedom Credit Card is well-suited for students or first-time users as it has a low annual fee, basic benefits, and relaxed eligibility criteria. It helps you build your credit history while offering savings on everyday expenses.
